clue.text: Loss of capital following summons by Nabokov

explanation.walkthrough: Capital here is the head; Nabokov's novel is 'Invitation to a Beheading', so a summons (invitation) is followed by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing one's head is decapitation, and the Nabokov title runs 'Invitation to a ...' with this word last.

explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke was a German-language lyric poet, author of the Duino Elegies.

clue.text: Wren made such a noble act

explanation.surface: Someone praises a wren for its noble deed.
explanation.walkthrough: Wren is P. C. Wren, the novelist who wrote 'Beau Geste', not the bird or the architect.
explanation.definitionFit: P. C. Wren wrote the Foreign Legion novel of this title, and the French phrase means a fine gesture.

clue.text: "will pledge you willingly in a cup of --" (Kenilworth)

parts.words: "will pledge you willingly in a cup of --" (Kenilworth)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Scott's novel Kenilworth; the missing word is an old sweet Spanish wine

explanation.walkthrough: In older usage the word names a sweet fortified wine, which is what Scott's character offers to drink in.
explanation.definitionFit: In Elizabethan English the word denoted a sweet Spanish wine, the drink pledged in the quoted line.

parts.note: a character, the Italian prince of Henry James's novel The Golden Bowl

explanation.walkthrough: 'Prince James' looks like royalty; James is the novelist Henry James, who created the prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James's novel The Golden Bowl centres on an impoverished Italian nobleman by this name.

explanation.surface: A French author catches sight of a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' reads as a verb (seen) but describes the animal's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Genet was a French novelist and playwright, and a genet is a spotted, cat-like mammal.

clue.text: Scary aunt somehow set straight by Faulkner

explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow set straight' rearranges SCARY AUNT; the definition is a book by William Faulkner.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctuary is a 1931 novel by William Faulkner.

explanation.walkthrough: The Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam, translated by Edward FitzGerald: 'Nor all thy Tears wash out a Word of it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verse says neither piety nor wit nor tears can blot out what has been written.

clue.text: Fifty per cent of actors reportedly like Mrs Rochester

explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Rochester is Bertha Mason of 'Jane Eyre', a Creole woman described in the dated term this answer uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha Mason, the first Mrs Rochester in Jane Eyre, is of mixed Creole descent.
